pairs.why: Both float the calculator on a pi-patterned yellow field, but B's pi motifs are softer and closer to the real card's quiet tone-on-tone; A's darker orange pi marks and edge vignette compete a little more.
The real card has a few small bubbles, one modest shell and two coins on a sand mound; A keeps the props smaller and quieter, while B's big bubbles, big pink shell and extra coin piles add clutter.
B uses a plain soft backdrop and a real wood floor like the real cards. A adds a high-contrast horseshoe pattern the real backdrops don't have, and that pattern competes with the barrel.
Both have the same quiet argyle backdrop and orange ground plane as the real card, and neither differs in staging or environment load.
Both float the fins on the same tone-on-tone concentric-circle field with no props, so staging gives no reason to choose.
A's desert is a few large quiet shapes (mesa, clouds, track, two bushes); B adds more small rocks, pebbles, track bolts and bushes, so it is busier than the real environments.
The real clock hangs on a striped wall with no floor. A matches that, while B adds a ledge and cast shadow strip that the real card doesn't have.
A keeps the full striped wall backdrop with the clock hanging on it, like the real card, while B invents a floor ledge with a ground shadow.
